paragraphs.source_en: Hirotada was already twenty years old and had three sons. Two of them had been born to Lady Aku, a concubine, and the other to Lady Odai, his former lawful wife. For a woman, marrying into a household that already had a legitimate heir naturally brought no small pressure.

paragraphs.source_en: When Maki-hime first heard of the marriage proposal, she meant to refuse it, but her father and elder brother would not allow her to. She had never dreamed of competing with Odai; as a woman, she had felt inferior to others from the outset. The lord of Okazaki was known throughout the Tokaido for his handsome, gallant ways, and day and night she worried whether she could win her husband's affection.

paragraphs.source_en: Her heart was filled with admiration for Lady Odai rather than jealousy of Lady Aku, and that admiration so preoccupied her that she scarcely noticed she had been brought to Nido Castle. Tahara itself was only a small castle. By comparison, Okazaki looked imposing, yet its interior was exceedingly plain. Maki-hime paid it no mind, supposing that most warrior households were like this. With that thought, she took her place.
